newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee trips offline during testing - NRC.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee trips offline during testing - NRC.

text.p: The 910 megawatt Maine Yankee nuclear power plant in Wiscasset, Maine was shutdown early Wednesday after tripping off line during testing, a spokeswoman for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.

"They tripped this morning at about 9:50 (EDT/1350 GMT) from 90 percent power," NRC spokeswoman Diane Screnci told Reuters. "They were doing testing on the reactor testing equipment. They're looking into what caused the trip."
Screnci said the plant, which operates at about 90 percent of capacity due to limitations imposed by the NRC, is in stable position in a hot shutdown.
Screnci said she did not know when the plant would be taken back on line.
Officials for Maine Yankee did not return phone calls.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power, 20 percent by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
Maine Governor Angus King said last week a comprehensive review by the NRC determined the plant was safe but was unlikely to return to full operating capacity in the near future.

NRC Chairwoman Shirley Ann Jackson, in the review released Tuesday said, "The economic pressures to contain costs and poor problem identification as a result of complacency and a lack of questioning attitude," caused the earlier problems.
